reviews.title: This product poisoned my cat - luckily he survived
reviews.text: I had been using Bravecto on my tabby cat for the last 4 years with no issues, apart from the awful toxic smell and my cat hating it, licking at the site profusely. This had me worried because I didn't want her to injest the treatment. A month ago, a week before Christmas, I applied a pipette of Bravecto to my other new tabby cat, Charles, who is over 3 kilos. This was the second time I was applying the treatment to him. A few days later he was extremely lethargic (very unusual for a male ginger cat) and then his left eye became cloudy. We brought him to the vet immediately for eye and blood tests. $450 later, we had no conclusive diagnosis but he had a very high fever and elevated liver values. The vet said to monitor my cat over the next phew days and administer an anti-inflammatory every day. His eye then developed a dark patch in his iris and we were getting so worried and upset. Thankfully the fever eased off, he got his energy back and the dark patch disappeared. I researched Bravecto and realised all of these symptoms came from this highly toxic pesticide: lethargy, fever, eye problems, elevated liver values. There are lots of articles on the web urging pet owners to avoid using Bravecto and petitions fighting for it to be taken off market. Never again will I be applying this poison to my babies. Please do not buy this product - do not risk your pet's health or life.
